newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa recovering but not out of danger.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa recovering but not out of danger.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Monday they were optimistic she will recover from her third heart surgery in five years, but cautioned that the 86-year-old nun was not out of danger.

"She is stable and we are very optimistic about her recovery," U.S. doctor Patricia Aubanel, a member of the medical team treating the renowned Roman Catholic missionary, told reporters at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.

Mother Teresa, considered by many as a living saint for her devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, had surgery on Friday to clear two blocked coronary arteries. She is also suffering kidney and lung problems, as well as pneumonia.
"Mother is still not out of danger and complications still may happen, but doctors this morning are optimistic," a medical bulletin issued by the hospital said.
Aubanel said doctors were now concentrating on Mother Teresa's kidney and lung problems, which the U.S. expert called the main concerns.
The hospital bulletin said that on Sunday, doctors were concerned that Mother Teresa's chronic lung disease, bronchial pneumonia and poor kidneys might set back her recovery.
"Continuous monitoring and support are being given so that other organs do not deteriorate while the heart is recovering," the medical bulletin said.
Aubanel said: "We are doing respiratory therapy for her lung problem and she is responding."
D.P. Shetty, chief of the medical team treating her, said on Sunday that Mother Teresa's heart pacemaker, fitted in 1989, had been reprogrammed.
"We have increased the heart rate of the pacemaker to strengthen the pumping of blood, which will support her kidneys to function better," Aubanel said on Monday.
She said the adjustment in the pacemaker had been a success and Mother Teresa was now urinating normally.
But asked when Mother Teresa might be allowed to return to her Missionaries of Charity religious order, Aubanel said: "It's too early to say when she will be released."

The medical bulletin said the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner said her prayers sitting in a chair, and was briefly visited by Vice-President Kocheril Raman Narayanan and the governor of West Bengal state, K.V. Raghunath Reddy.

Mother Teresa told Aubanel to work hard, and the U.S. doctor replied that the renowned nun also had to work hard to get well, the bulletin said. "That is my duty, so I will do," it quoted Mother Teresa as saying.
She has undergone heart surgery twice -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
Nuns at the Calcutta headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity, which has about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries and was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949, have held prayers for her recovery.
